The View Transitions API itself is native and GPU-composited, and the animation only runs once per click (not continuously), so the baseline cost is already low for a simple content site like this one. content.text:
Real but modest risk: mobile GPUs (especially mid/low-range Android) have less fill-rate than desktop, and recomputing a radial-gradient mask across the full screen every frame at high DPR (2–3x on most phones) is exactly the kind of paint-heavy work that can drop frames there, even though it's fine on desktop. Two things already protect the worst case: unsupported browsers (older iOS Safari) fall back to an instant swap, and `prefers-reduced-motion` skips the animation entirely. But supported mobile browsers (Chrome/Safari on recent phones) still pay the full gradient cost.

Cheapest fix that keeps your preferred look on desktop: swap to the lighter `clip-path` circle (geometric, no gradient sampling) only for touch devices, via `(pointer: coarse)`, and leave the soft gradient mask as-is for mouse/trackpad.
